title: Brazilian top-flight player handed 12-game suspension for sexist remarks
content:
A sports court in Brazil has suspended Red Bull Bragantino defender Gustavo Marques for 12 matches after he made sexist remarks about a female referee.

Marques, 24, was also fined in 30,000 Brazilian reais ($5,700, £4,277) for his comments about referee Daiane Muniz after his side’s 2-1 defeat to Sao Paulo in a Sao Paulo state league game on February 21.

The Sao Paulo State Sports Justice Tribunal (TJD-SP) ban only applies to state-run competitions, so will not prevent Marques from playing in the Brazilian league or national cup competition.

The player was reported for violating articles 243G and 243F of the Brazilian Code of Sports Justice (CBJD), referencing discriminatory acts and offences.

The defender, on loan at the Brazilian club from Benfica, publicly criticised the competition’s organisers for “allowing a woman to referee a game of this size” in a post-match interview.

“I think the FPF (Sao Paulo Football Federation) has to look at a game of this size and not appoint a female referee,” he said.

“With all respect to women around the world — I’m married, I also have my mum — I’m sorry if I’m saying anything bad about women, but I don’t think that she has the capacity to referee this game.”

After the interview, his club RB Bragantino said “nothing justifies” the player’s remarks, banned him from selection for their next game — against Sao Paulo — and added he would be “fined 50 per cent of his total earnings”.

The Athletic has approached RB Bragantino following Thursday’s ruling from the Sao Paulo court.

Marques subsequently apologised, telling reporters in the mixed zone at the Cicero De Souza Marques stadium that he wanted “to ask forgiveness from the referee and her assistant.”

“I’m here once again to apologise to women around the world and here in Brazil,” he said, per ESPN Brazil. “I said things that I shouldn’t have in that moment about Daiane.

“I went to her to apologise afterwards, and to her assistant as well. So I’m here again to apologise to women around the world, there are plenty of women here too; I hope they can forgive me for what I said.

“I’m upset, I’m sad, my wife has already scolded me, my mother as well. So I’m here to say sorry. I’m a man, a human being, and humans make mistakes.”

RB Bragantino is part of the Red Bull network of clubs, which includes RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga, Austria’s Red Bull Salzburg and Major League Soccer side New York Bulls.
